title: Book One · Chapter 44: Bo's New Bell
story:
A low clang comes from the road outside Mr Qiu's stall. Ronan looks up from a row of erasers.

Bo is holding the red bicycle. There is a new black bell on its handlebar. Mr Han stands beside him with a shopping bag.

“It sounds like a pot,” Leo says.

Bo presses it again. “A very good pot.”

Mr Qiu puts a hand over his tea cup. “Not this one, I hope.”

Ronan hears the joke and smiles. The red bicycle is clean. The pale mark on the wheel is still there. He remembers that wall and the mark. But the bike still belongs to Bo.

Bo asks about the kite. Dad told Mr Han about the first good flight. Leo shows Bo the flight with his hands. He lifts his arms to show the turns. He tells him about the falls, too. Ronan did not expect him to tell that part.

Mum is there for needles. Mr Han is waiting for a shoe repair farther down the street. The adults give the children permission to play. The small square beside the stall is free. The bicycle stays against the wall with Mr Han.

Bo draws a circle in chalk. He has a little wooden spinning top in his pocket. Its point is smooth. Bo puts it on the flat stone. He gives it a quick turn. “Try it like that,” he says.

Leo tries first. The top falls on its side. Ronan gets it moving, but only for two short turns. Bo's turn lasts much longer.

“You knew this game first,” Leo says.

“Yes,” Bo says. “Yes. Now I can show you.”

Ronan laughs. Leo looks cross for one second, then asks for another go.

After a while, Bo looks at the bicycle again.

“Is your bell loud?” he asks Ronan.

“It has a bright, clear sound.”

“Could we trade? I hear mine on the road. Its sound is too low for me.”

Mr Han hears and looks over. “You can ask. The answer belongs to Ronan.”

Ronan looks at Bo's new black bell. They could change bells. Then his old bell would be on the red bike again. He thinks about that for a moment.

But the bike would still be Bo's.

“No,” he says.

Bo rolls the top between his hands. “All right.”

He doesn't argue. Ronan was ready to give three reasons. But Bo accepts his no. Ronan can stop explaining.

“You can hear it one day,” he adds.

“I'd like that.”

Mum calls them to wash the chalk from their fingers. Mr Qiu brings a small basin, but they use only a little water. Bo has grey dust on his nose. Leo sees it first. He lets Bo walk around for a minute. Then he tells Bo about the dust.

“That costs you a turn,” Bo says.

“Whose rule?”

“My nose's.”

They laugh together. For a moment, the bicycle is only a red shape by the wall. Ronan doesn't forget it. He can watch the spinning top, too.

Bo is ready to leave. “Can we play again next week?” he asks. “Ask nearer the day,” Mum says. Mr Han agrees. They do not promise a day yet. Bo will ask his father later. Ronan will ask Mum, too.

At home, Ronan presses his own bell once. It sounds brighter than Bo's. Ronan smiles at its familiar sound. He sets it back on the soft cloth.

Dad sits beside him. “Are you all right?” he asks. “You saw the red bicycle again today.”

“Bo asked to trade bells.”

“What did you say?”

“No.”

Dad nods and waits. Ronan is quiet for a moment. Then he remembers the wooden top.

“Can we make a circle on the yard stones? We can choose a place clear of the path.”

“Ask Mrs Lan about the chalk,” Dad says.

Ronan goes to ask. He wants to play with a top now.
studyGuide:
---

重点表达：trade＝交换；bell＝铃；chalk＝粉笔；turn＝一次轮到自己。

理解问题：

1. Bo 的新车铃和 Ronan 的旧铃有什么不同？
2. Ronan 为什么拒绝交换，却仍能和 Bo 一起玩？
